grader.scenario: Double charge for pay-per-view boxing match on TV set-top box bill
grader.notes: Neil handles security verification and acknowledges Kasim's frustration over a duplicate £24.95 pay-per-view charge. However, he exhibits multiple severe technical and soft skill faults: he fails to paraphrase, abdicates ownership to third-party clearinghouses, accuses the customer of 'mashing the red button', repeats an order question already answered, and leaves the financial dispute unresolved with a 5-7 day waiting period.

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: Customer experienced an outburst of frustration at turn 34 ([07:17]) ('What do you mean it's not handled by your team? You are S-Net, you send me the bill, and you took fifty pounds instead of twenty-five!'), but Agent never acknowledged it, responding defensively at turn 35 ([07:33]) with an accusatory remark.

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: Agent never restated the core issue in his own words; only confirmed contact email at turn 50.

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: [01:10] Customer: 'I ordered it through the red button on our main S-Net TV 4K box in the living room.' followed by Agent at [07:45]: 'How did you order the boxing event on Saturday evening?'

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: [01:50] Agent: 'pay-per-view event billing is cleared through Sky Box Office and DAZN partner merchant systems, so duplicate authorization disputes are governed by external partner rules and are not handled directly by our front-line team.'

items.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
items.evidence: [06:40] Agent: 'If you mash the red button multiple times during a live broadcast, obviously you risk triggering duplicate purchase transactions.'

items.name: Confirmed the issue is resolved
items.evidence: [09:15] The £24.95 duplicate charge remained on the account; customer was told to wait 5-7 business days for an email review and ended the call dissatisfied.
